newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to offer 26-30 pct stake in Raba.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to offer 26-30 pct stake in Raba.

text.p: Hungary plans to place a stake of 26 to 30 percent in axle maker Raba Rt privately with financial and strategic investors, as the first stage of the company's privatisation, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
"The government decided today that the state-owned stake in Raba will be sold in two stages," Prime Minister's Office Secretary of State Elemer Kiss told a news conference.

In the first phase of the sale, each investor will be allowed to acquire a maximum stake of between five and 10 percent, and those bidders will be preferred which undertake to raise Raba's capital, Kiss said.

Kiss said the state privatisation agency APV held a 37.05 percent stake in Raba, and it had an agreement with the state-owned Hungarian Development Bank to take over the bank's 49.68 percent stake in the axle-maker.
He said local municipalities held 16.5 percent of Raba and maximum 10 percent of the state-owned shares would be offered to Raba employees at preferential prices.
The state will publicly offer its remaining shares to Hungarian small investors as well as domestic and foreign institutional investors, Kiss said.
He added that the privatisation must prepare Raba for listing it on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
Privatisation minister Judit Csiha said last week that an at least 30 percent stake in Raba will be offered for sale in September at the earliest.
Kiss declined to disclose further information about the timing of the offerings, but said the APV should prepare for the first stage of the privatisation as quickly as possible.
